key_insight: vid2vid-long uses explicit correspondences across video frames to help translated videos stay consistent over time. This addresses a key limitation of methods that can only look back through a fixed-length window.
problem_solved: Fast video-to-video models can lose visual consistency when relevant earlier frames fall outside their context window, making long-running interactive applications harder to support.
method: Introduce vid2vid-long, a correspondence-based approach to video-to-video translation.
Use explicit cross-frame correspondences to connect related visual content over time.
Target long-range temporal consistency beyond the history available in a fixed-length causal window.
impact: The approach could help practitioners build interactive video translation systems with more stable visual appearance over longer sequences. The provided abstract is truncated and does not include implementation details or measured results.
visual_elements: A video timeline showing relevant earlier content falling outside a fixed-length context window.
Arrows linking corresponding objects or regions across widely separated frames.
A side-by-side schematic contrasting appearance drift with temporally consistent translation.
A pipeline diagram: input video → cross-frame correspondences → translated video.
paper_title: Consistent Video-to-Video Translation via Explicit Correspondences
paper_authors: Gaurav Parmar, Zhengqi Li, Richard Zhang, Jun-Yan Zhu, Srinivasa Narasimhan
